corpus: Solid Waste Management Rules, 2026 (S.O. 388(E)), gazetted 28 Jan 2026 (Gazette CG-DL-E-28012026-269620); rules in force 1 Apr 2026. Household and commercial source segregation into wet / dry / sanitary / special-care streams.

rows.rule_text: Households must segregate wet waste (kitchen waste, vegetables, fruit peels, meat, flowers) for composting or bio-methanation at the nearest facility.
Commercial generators must segregate wet waste and ensure its composting or bio-methanation, or process on-site as far as possible under Extended Bulk Waste Generator Responsibility.
Households must segregate dry waste (plastic, paper, metal, glass, wood, rubber) for transport to Material Recovery Facilities for sorting and recycling.

Commercial generators must segregate dry waste and ensure its transport to MRFs, with Bulk Waste Generators (floor area 20,000 m² or more, water consumption 40,000 L/day or more, or solid waste generation 100 kg/day or more) required to process wet waste on-site or obtain an EBWGR certificate.
Households must securely wrap and store sanitary waste (used diapers, sanitary towels, tampons, condoms) separately for designated collection.

Commercial generators must securely wrap and store sanitary waste separately, with Bulk Waste Generators (floor area 20,000 m² or more, water consumption 40,000 L/day or more, or solid waste generation 100 kg/day or more) required to obtain an EBWGR certificate where on-site processing is not feasible.
Households must deposit special-care waste (paint cans, bulbs, mercury thermometers, medicines) through authorised agencies or at designated collection centres.

Commercial generators must ensure special-care waste (paint cans, bulbs, medicines) is collected by authorised agencies or deposited at designated centres; Bulk Waste Generators must obtain an EBWGR certificate for such streams where decentralised processing is not feasible.
